title: Ops buffer scenario mapping & price-shock response playbook
content:
Summary:
This is an operational playbook mapping a 90–180 day buffer of spend and headcount actions to a set of pricing shock scenarios. The goal is to give Finance, GTM, and Eng-ops a short runbook to reduce burn quickly while preserving core throughput for highest-value customers. This doc combines lightweight sensitivity math, concrete trigger thresholds, and step-by-step mitigations that can be executed inside 7–30 days.

Purpose and audience:
- Purpose: define a repeatable set of actions (with estimated cost savings and downstream risks) that can be executed on price shocks or demand contractions.
- Audience: CFO, Head of GTM, VP Eng, Head of Dedicated & Private, People Ops, Revenue Ops.

Quick recommendation (executive TL;DR):
- Prepare three playbooks: (1) 7-day rapid cost triage, (2) 30-day capacity rebalancing, (3) 90-day structural pricing/commit play.
- Pre-authorize Head of Finance + VP Eng to pause non-critical hires under threshold A. Pre-authorize CRO to implement temporary slab pricing & commit discounts under threshold B.
- Maintain a 10% ops buffer (unallocated commit capacity) by default to limit forced fallbacks.

Assumptions (base numbers used in sensitivity math):
- Current monthly cash burn (net): $5.2M.
- Token-related variable infra cost (incl. GPU, cloud egress, third-party): $0.30 / 1M tokens (weighted avg across hosted + dedicated).
- Billable tokens / month: 200B tokens.
- Average revenue / 1M tokens: $2.40 (weighted average of hosted, dedicated, and private).
- Committed reserved capacity discounts currently deliver ~25% lower infra unit cost vs spot/hosted.
- Hiring pipeline: 18 open roles slated to start across Eng/Recruiting/Support over next 60 days (aggregate OTE run-rate impact: $0.95M / month once onboarded).

Scenario definitions and one-line impacts:
1) Mild price shock (S1): 10% realized reduction in revenue velocity (usage).
   - Revenue delta: -10% of token-driven rev = ~$480k / month.
   - Immediate action: freeze non-critical contractor spend (~$120k/month savings) + defer 4 hires (saves ~ $200k/month once onboarded). Net ~ $320k/month retained; runway +0.6 months.

2) Moderate price + price-squeeze (S2): 20% drop in usage + 5% downward pressure on list price (mix shift to cheaper tiers).
   - Rev delta: ~-25% effective revenue on token income = -$1.2M / month.
   - Immediate action: implement 30-day slab pricing for new customers (protect committed customers), pause all non-essential hiring, cut discretionary S&M spend by 25% (~$300k), shift burst capacity to lower-cost cloud region (saves ~ $150k/month). Estimated savings month-1: $650k. Balance needed: consider a temporary 5% price uplift for new enterprise offers or accelerated commits.

3) Severe multi-quarter shock (S3): 40% usage drop + pricing competition forces 15% realized avg price reduction.
   - Rev delta: ~-55% = ~$2.64M / month.
   - Immediate action: trigger 60–90 day restructuring plan: selective furloughs/hiring freeze (targeted $1.2M monthly savings), renegotiate dedicated capacity contracts, accelerate Optimize toolkit releases that reduce unit infra cost by 20% (target $400k/month). Requires board-level approval for structural actions.

Headcount phasing matrix (impacted universe = 18 open reqs + 12 roles in hiring pipeline) - illustrative numbers:
- Pause threshold A (mild): freeze 4 open reqs (Eng infra x2, Solutions x1, Sales AE x1). Estimated monthly avoided run-rate when filled: $200k.
- Pause threshold B (moderate): freeze + cancel additional 8 reqs (adds $450k avoided).
- Structural threshold C (severe): initiate targeted role reductions / voluntary buyouts (target $1.2M run-rate).

Cost sensitivity quick table (text form):
- Unit revenue per 1M tokens = $2.40; unit cost = $0.30. Gross margin per 1M tokens = $2.10.
- If realized avg price falls 10% => revenue per 1M = $2.16 => gross margin = $1.86 => margin loss = $0.24 per 1M => for 200B tokens = $48k/month loss per 1B tokens -> scaled to scenario above.

Pricing levers and expected near-term impact: (each lever includes operational friction and risk)
- Short-term slab pricing (7–14 days): introduce limited-term reduced feature slab for new low-touch customers. Impact: prevents broad price cascade, estimated +$0.2–0.5M / month revenue protection with minimal ops risk.
- Commit accelerator coupons (30 days): small discounts for 6–12 month commits to secure monthly cash. Impact: front-loaded cash but potential ARR dilution; expected +$0.5M cash in month-1 for 10–15% of pipeline.
- Temporary enterprise uplift (targeted 5–10% price uplift for high-SLA contracts): requires legal & sales alignment; can recover $0.3–0.6M/month with churn risk.

Operational quick actions (7-day runbook):
1) Finance: switch to weekly burn reporting, reforecast runway daily for 30 days.
2) GTM: pause new channel spend; triage top 30 prospects and accelerate commit offers.
3) Eng: postpone non-critical infra changes, enact autoscaling cost caps for non-prod clusters.
4) People Ops: pause all offers not pre-approved by CFO + People Lead.
5) Sales Ops: enable 30-day commit coupons and slab offers, track conversion rate.

30-day capacity rebalancing (30-day runbook):
- Move 15% of burst capacity to cheaper regions; target 10–15% unit cost reduction on burst.
- Apply application-level caching / prefix caching aggressively for top 25 customers (expected token reduction 8–12%).
- Enable lower-precision quant profiles on non-critical models deployed to hosted pool (saves ~6–9% on GPU hour cost).

90-day structural items (90-day runbook):
- Evaluate converting a portion of Hosted customers to Commit contracts with tapered discounts.
- Close renegotiation of large dedicated contracts to add more flexible burst terms.
- Prioritize Optimize roadmap items that reduce infra by >15% and ship them early.

Decision triggers (metrics to watch, thresholds):
- Metric A: Monthly net cash runway < 9 months -> trigger 7-day runbook.
- Metric B: QoQ billed tokens fall >12% or rev down >10% -> trigger 30-day rebalancing + hiring freeze.
- Metric C: QoQ billed tokens fall >30% or realized avg price down >12% -> trigger 90-day structural + board notification.

Risk table (short):
- Customer churn risk: medium when lifting price for new enterprise offers.
- Product velocity risk: delaying hires slows key roadmap items (Optimize, Dedicated autoscale).
- Reputational risk: public price changes may invite competitive response.

Communications and approvals:
- Pre-approve two-tier signoff: Tier-1 (CFO + VP Eng) for actions <= $400k/month; Tier-2 (CEO + Board Chair) for structural actions > $400k/month recurring.
- Communication cadence: 48-hour internal all-hands for affected teams, weekly exec readout until stability restored.

Tracking workbook (suggested tabs in a live sheet):
- Tab 1: Weekly burn & runway model (inputs: cash balance, monthly burn components, savings enacted).
- Tab 2: Headcount live tracker (offers, starts, freezes, OTE delta).
- Tab 3: Pricing sensitivity engine (inputs: token volumes by customer cohort, price per 1M, elasticity assumptions).
- Tab 4: Action tracker (owner, ETA, expected monthly impact, status).

Next steps (for this doc):
- Finance to convert the above into a working Google Sheet (owner: Ravi Patel) with the tabs above by EOD +3 (2026-02-13).
- Eng + Optimize leads to provide quick list of 3 prioritizable infra changes with estimated % cost impact by EOD +7.
- GTM to prepare two commit coupon templates and legal-approved T&Cs within 10 days.

Review notes / open questions:
- Need better measurement of live elasticity by cohort (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Confirm legal constraints on temporary pricing changes for existing contracts (Elena to confirm).
- Consider pre-negotiating hot fallback capacity with cloud partners for a capped dollar amount.

Appendix (short worked example):
- If a 20% usage drop hits (S2) and we implement the 30-day slab + hiring pause + regional shift, month-1 savings estimated: $650k. Remaining gap from $1.2M rev delta = $550k. If commit coupons convert 10% pipeline ($500k cash) then net immediate gap is ~ $50k. That buys time to negotiate dedicated margins and ship Optimize savings.

Document history:
- Drafted 2026-02-10 by Daniela Ortiz; version iterated with Ravi Patel & Elena Kirov 2026-02-18 and 2026-03-04.
